problems.title: Unbounded OLS estimates invalidate capped-incentive target selection

source_claim.location: PDF p46 LemmaG.6; p9 §5; p41 Algorithm7 lines6,10-12 and Eq45; pp42-44 AppG.2-G.3
source_claim.paraphrase: Conditioning on E, every targeted arm receives an offer strictly exceeding its optimal incentive; proof bounds ||s_hat|| by d and optimal incentive by2d.

assumptions: A={+1,-1}, s*=-1, nu*=0, initial estimate0; all in unit ball and A spans R
Agent greedily maximizes ordinary least-squares estimate plus incentive
First agent noise is equiprobable Rademacher ±1; all later noises and all principal noises0; these are conditionally1-subgaussian
Phase1 uses exact G-design rho(+1)=rho(-1)=1/2 and targets+1 first
Probability1/2 branch has initial noise-1; E holds throughout subsequent path

Algorithm8 initial-width2 requires the intended dyadic extension i=-1 (z=1/4), absent from its stated natural-number indices; under that reading it immediately breaks at epsilon0=1 before any observations. Literal nonnegative indexing leaves initialization undefined.
problems.check: First target reward-2 yields OLS-2. Next+1 target requires incentive4; algorithm offers2+1/T. Agent scores are1/T for+1 and2 for-1. For all later observations U=n, error=-1/n; E-agent holds analytically and E-principal is exact. Variant A={1,-1/4} with rho half each has maximum leverage32/17<2, required incentive5/2 and actual Gram increment1/16 instead of intended1.
problems.result: LemmaG.6 fails on an admissible positive-probability event inside E.
counterevidence: Bounded true parameter does not bound unprojected OLS estimates.
Only initial estimate is constrained by unit ball; no subsequent clipping found.
The symmetric-arm witness preserves scalar Gram increments by coincidence; the valid C2-design variant removes that coincidence.
This does not establish that the asymptotic regret rate itself is false.
The preceding-search execution is conditional on the explicitly disclosed intended i=-1 extension; the source's literal index range is itself incomplete.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem5.1 proof pp43-44 uses LemmaG.6 for target/actual-arm equivalence, designed counts and subsequent error and elimination bounds; these are substantive dependencies.

correction.note: An explicit bounded-estimator model would restore this cap step but changes the agent behavior; full theorem repair not established.

acceptance_check.truth_and_assumptions: The closed unit ball constrains true parameters and the initial estimate, not later unconstrained OLS. The Rademacher-first-noise/zero-later-noise construction meets the linear model and stated good event.
acceptance_check.decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence: The first reward -2 produces OLS -2; the next target requires 4 but receives at most 2+1/T. The asymmetric {1,-1/4} variant changes the actual Gram increment from 1 to 1/16. The report explicitly retains Algorithm 8's undefined natural initial index and uses the disclosed intended i=-1 extension for the execution witness.
acceptance_check.core_dependency_and_severity: Major: Lemma G.6's invalid norm bound and target-selection conclusion support the core linear regret derivation. No claim that the regret rate is unattainable or that the separate i.i.d. theorem fails is needed.
acceptance_check.correction_scope: Projected/bounded OLS would alter the stated agent model and need further proofs; a complete theorem repair is not verified.

problems.title: Algorithm3 exceeds the exact2ceil(log2T) round bound

source_claim.location: PDF p6 Lemma3.1, p18 LemmaD.6, p14 Algorithm3

assumptions: Two bounded iid constant-reward arms: target0, competitor q=2^{-(L-1)}-2^{-2L}
Competitor has previously been sampled, target empirical mean0; reachable from Algorithm1 zero initialization by listing competitor first
Greedy agent; all comparisons strict; no exploration or tie convention needed
problems.check: L-1 successful midpoints1/2,...,h with h=2^{-(L-1)}, followed byL failed midpoints h(1-2^{-j}) andL successful checks at h. C1 stopping test is only in success branch; C2 reachesL at return line17.
problems.result: Exactly3L-1 offer rounds:47 rather than stated32 atL=16.
counterevidence: Returned incentive in this instance remains close to optimal.
3L-1 is still O(logT); this does not refute the stated regret orders.
The original proof's all-fail-midpoint case omits prior successful midpoint rounds.
problems.core_dependency: Local exact runtime bound only; no material dependence of the asymptotic conclusions is demonstrated.

correction.note: No universal sharp revised bound certified; example gives a lower bound on the worst-case constant.

acceptance_check.truth_and_assumptions: The constant bounded-reward construction is admissible and Algorithm 3's two counters permit more than the exact 2*ceil(log2(T)) rounds.
acceptance_check.decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence: For L=16, the exact transcript has (L-1)+2L=47 rounds versus 32. No tie is needed; returned incentive accuracy and O(log T) duration survive.
acceptance_check.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor: a false exact constant in the duration argument, without demonstrated damage to the asymptotic regret order.
acceptance_check.correction_scope: A universal sharp replacement bound is not claimed.

overall_impact: Major applies to the demonstrated invalid linear derivation; Minor applies independently to the precise search duration. No whole-paper invalidity claim.
